relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with primary CoQ10 deficiency caused by biallelic PDSS1 variants (COQ10D2), expanding the phenotype.

findings.statement: Bellusci et al. (2021) gave a detailed clinical description of a boy with primary CoQ10 deficiency due to biallelic PDSS1 mutations, who had been born prematurely after in vitro fertilization in a pregnancy complicated by twin-twin transfusion. At 5 months of age he had failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and chronic distal phalangeal erythema. The disease progressed to a multisystem disorder with severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy, nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, cystic white matter changes, and chronic heart failure, and he died at 3 years of age. Brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy at 12 months and, at 24 months, small necrotic or porencephalic cysts in the white matter around the lateral ventricles and in the commissural fibers.
quotes: At the age of 5 months, he presented failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and distal phalangeal erythema (Figure 1).

However, he developed a progressive multisystem disorder with severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy and nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, white matter cystic change and chronic heart failure. He died at the age of 3 years old.
White matter tracts surrounding the lateral ventricles and commissural fibres had signal abnormalities, showing small necrotic or porencephalic cysts.

findings.statement: In the PDSS1 patient described by Bellusci et al. (2021), laboratory tests showed anemia, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, tricarboxylic aciduria, and reduced CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes. The authors stated that this was the first reported patient with PDSS1 mutations with 3-methylglutaconic aciduria.
quotes: Laboratory tests showed anemia, lactic acidosis, 3‐methyl‐glutaconic, and tricarboxylic aciduria and decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes.
This is the first reported patient with PDSS1 mutations presenting with 3-methyl-glutaconic aciduria and distal phalangeal erythema, expanding the phenotype of primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.

findings.statement: Bellusci et al. (2021) found biallelic mutations in the PDSS1 gene in their patient with primary CoQ10 deficiency: c.716T>G (p.Val239Gly) and c.1183C>T (p.Arg395Ter) (NM_014317.3).
quotes: Three months later, when biallelic PDSS1 mutations were identified (NM_014317.3: c.716 T > G (p.Val239Gly) and NM_014317.3: c.1183C > T (p.Arg395*)), ubidecarenone was increased to 30 mg/kg/day.

findings.statement: Bellusci et al. (2021) started oral ubidecarenone (CoQ10) at 15 mg/kg/day at 5 months of age and raised it to 30 mg/kg/day after the genetic diagnosis. This high-dose supplementation did not halt disease progression, and the patient died at 3 years of age.
quotes: At this time, oral ubidecarenone was started at 15 mg/kg/day.
Supplementation with high dose of coenzyme Q10 was not effective to control disease progression and the patient died at the age of 3 years old because of a progressive multisystem disorder.

findings.statement: Bellusci et al. (2021) suggested that the combination of phalangeal erythema, livedo reticularis, and pulmonary hypertension in their PDSS1 patient pointed to microvascular dysfunction as a possible underlying mechanism.
quotes: The coexistence in our case of phalangeal erythema, livedo reticularis, and pulmonary hypertension suggests microvascular dysfunction as a possible underlying physiopathogenic mechanism.

relevance_reason: Reports a new family with homozygous PDSS1 missense variant causing COQ10D2 (deafness followed by optic atrophy).

findings.statement: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported a 16-year-old girl born to consanguineous Egyptian parents who had severe language delay and profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss diagnosed at age 4 years, later mild intellectual disability, and progressive visual loss from age 11-14 years with visual acuity of 1/10 bilaterally, red-green dyschromatopsia, and optic atrophy predominantly in the inferior temporal sector. VEP showed increased P100 latency and reduced amplitude, and OCT showed bilateral reduction in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. She also had diffuse mild muscle weakness, mild postural tremor of the upper limbs, normal brain MRI, and a moderately dysplastic mitral valve with moderate insufficiency, tricuspid insufficiency, and a moderately dilated left atrium.
quotes: This 16‐year‐old girl was born to consanguineous Egyptian parents following an uneventful pregnancy.
At the age of 4 years, a profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was found and treated with an externally powered prosthesis.

Fundus examination showed optic atrophy prevalent in the inferior temporal sector, visual‐evoked potentials (VEP) documented an increase in latency and a reduction in amplitude of the P100 waveform in both eyes.

phenotypes.text: reduced retinal nerve fiber layer thickness
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal retinal nerve fiber layer morphology

findings.statement: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported that the 6-year-old younger sister of the proband had bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and, at age 6 years, developed decreased visual acuity with optic atrophy (bilateral temporal pallor of the optic nerve head) and divergent strabismus; she also had mild intellectual disability and muscular involvement. In both sisters sensorineural deafness preceded optic atrophy, and lactic acidosis, macrocephaly, peripheral neuropathy, and nephrotic syndrome were absent.
quotes: her 6‐year‐old sister suffered bilateral sensorineural hearing loss

The affected sister, at the age of 6 years, developed a decrease in visual acuity and a following ophthalmological examination revealed an optic atrophy, with bilaterally pallor of the optic nerve head on the temporal sector at fundus examination, and divergent strabismus.
Notably, in these cases, neurosensorial loss preceded optic atrophy, like in our cases.

findings.statement: In 2 Egyptian sisters, born to consanguineous parents, with sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, Nardecchia et al. (2021) identified a homozygous missense variant in the PDSS1 gene, c.735G-T (p.Gln245His), by whole-exome sequencing. The variant, at a highly conserved residue, lay within a 12-Mb region of homozygosity, was absent from gnomAD, and segregated with the disorder: both parents were heterozygous, an unaffected brother was heterozygous, and an unaffected sister was homozygous wildtype. Sanger sequencing of OPA1, OPA3, and WFS1 was negative.
quotes: A whole‐exome sequencing analysis revealed a homozygous likely pathogenic missense variant c.735G > T in the PDSS1 gene, never reported in the public database GnomAD. This variant causes the amino acid change p.Gln245His, in a highly conserved position (98.5%, Fig. 1A).
The variant lies in a long region of homozygosity (12 Mb) and its segregation was confirmed in her parents (I:1 and I:2).
the unaffected sister (II:2) and brother (II:3) was, respectively, homozygous wild‐type and heterozygous for the variant (Fig. 1).

findings.statement: Nardecchia et al. (2021) noted that visual system involvement in CoQ10 deficiency has been reported only in defects of the earliest steps of CoQ10 synthesis, with optic atrophy in PDSS1 deficiency, and that, in contrast to OPA1 and OPA3 defects, sensorineural deafness appears to precede optic atrophy in PDSS1 deficiency. They suggested PDSS1 deficiency be included in the differential diagnosis of optic atrophy with sensorineural deafness as a potentially treatable condition.
quotes: Visual system involvement in CoQ10 deficiencies has been reported only in the defect of the very first steps of CoQ10 synthesis and it consists of optic atrophy, a combination of optic atrophy and retinitis pigmentosa or retinitis pigmentosa only in PDSS1, PDSS2, and COQ2 defect, respectively.
In contrast to OPA1 and OPA3 defects, the onset of sensorineural deafness seems to precede the optic atrophy in PDSS1, hallmarking this particular form.

relevance_reason: The abstract says variants in PDSS1, the gene behind COQ10D2, turned up in a targeted next-generation sequencing cohort of patients with suspected mitochondrial disease. It gives no details about the patients or the variants.

findings.statement: Vasta et al. (2012) performed targeted next-generation sequencing of the exons of 908 known and candidate nuclear genes in 26 patients with known or suspected mitochondrial disorders. Among the variants they found in known pathogenic genes were variants in PDSS1, alongside variants in CPT2, POLG, UBE3A, and SDHD. The authors concluded that the diagnostic spectrum of mitochondrial disorders is much broader than previously thought.
quotes: Targeted next-generation sequencing was performed on 26 patients with known or suspected mitochondrial disorders using in-solution capture for the exons of 908 known and candidate nuclear genes and an Illumina genome analyzer.
Instead, several variants in known pathogenic genes including CPT2, POLG, PDSS1, UBE3A, SDHD, and a few potentially pathogenic variants in candidate genes such as MTO1 or SCL7A13 were identified.

relevance_reason: Reports the identification of a homozygous PDSS1 mutation (D308E) in a family with CoQ10 deficiency, with mapping by homozygosity and functional yeast complementation, which establishes COQ10D2.

findings.statement: Mollet et al. (2007) studied 2 families with inborn errors of CoQ10 biosynthesis. In both, quinone-dependent oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) activities were in the range of the lowest control values, while OXPHOS enzyme activities themselves were normal. Adding quinone restored normal OXPHOS activities, which confirmed CoQ10 deficiency.
quotes: In both cases, enzymologic studies showed that quinone-dependent OXPHOS activities were in the range of the lowest control values, while OXPHOS enzyme activities were normal.
CoQ10 deficiency was confirmed by restoration of normal OXPHOS activities after addition of quinone.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain

findings.statement: In family 1, Mollet et al. (2007) did a genome-wide search for homozygosity and identified a region on chromosome 10. This region contains PDSS1, the human ortholog of yeast COQ1, which encodes a key enzyme of CoQ10 synthesis.
quotes: A genome-wide search for homozygosity in family 1 identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1), which encodes the human ortholog of the yeast COQ1 gene, a key enzyme of CoQ10 synthesis.

findings.statement: In family 1 with CoQ10 deficiency, Mollet et al. (2007) sequenced PDSS1 and identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution that changes a conserved amino acid (D308E). When yeast Delta-coq1 strains were transformed with the corresponding mutant yeast COQ1 gene, they grew poorly on respiratory medium. The authors concluded that the mutation causes the OXPHOS deficiency.
quotes: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).

Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively, resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium, indicating that these mutations are indeed the cause of OXPHOS deficiency.

findings.statement: In a second family with CoQ10 deficiency, Mollet et al. (2007) sequenced COQ2 directly and identified a single-base-pair frameshift deletion (c.1198delT, N401fsX415) that results in a premature stop codon. Mutant human COQ2 did not support growth of yeast Delta-coq2 strains on respiratory medium. This shows that CoQ10 deficiency is genetically heterogeneous.
quotes: In the second family, direct sequencing of OH-benzoate polyprenyltransferase (COQ2), the human ortholog of the yeast COQ2 gene, identified a single base pair frameshift deletion resulting in a premature stop codon (c.1198delT, N401fsX415).
